dct_description_sm: The Streams Project at the Toolik Field Station has been monitoring physical, chemical, and biological parameters in a 5-km, fourth-order reach of the Kuparuk River near its intersection with the Dalton Highway and the Trans-Alaska Pipeline. In 1989, similar studies were begun on a 3.5-km, third-order reach of a second stream, Oksrukuyik Creek. In each river, physical conditions (such as discharge and temperature), nutrient levels, primary production, insects, and fishes are monitored throughout the summer.
dct_subject_sm: Social sciences, economics and policy -> Environment surveillance
dct_title_s: Arctic Long Term Ecological Research (LTER): Streams in Alaska
